newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends lower on commercial demand.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends lower on commercial demand.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended slightly lower against its U.S. counterpart after a day of narrow range trading on Monday, reflecting routine commercial demand for the U.S. dollar, dealers said.
The local unit finished at T$27.862 against Saturday's T$27.842 close. Turnover through dealers was US$162.5 million.
Dealers said the Taiwan dollar remained in a downtrend but would not immediately test eight-year support at T$28 due to expectations that central bank intervention would be likely.

Despite central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong's pledge on Saturday that the bank would not intervene in the foreign exchange market, dealers said the market believed the central bank would try to smooth any depreciation.
"The market had watched as the central bank intervened while maintaining its standard line of non-intervention. Why should it be different this time?" said one dealer at a foreign bank.

"Every time the Taiwan dollar seems to touch T$27.90, intervention orchestrated by the central bank emerges. There has been little speculation today because the market is convinced the central bank will intervene," the dealer said.
A May 30 Reuters Poll of senior Taipei dealers appeared to support the market's general perception.
Four of six dealers polled said Taiwan's easing dollar was likely to break eight-year support at T$28 in the third quarter, citing slack economic growth and political uncertainties.
All six cautioned that the central bank was determined to defend the Taiwan dollar's stability to prevent an acceleration of capital outflows that would hurt Taiwan people's confidence.
Two of the six said the central bank's defence would be so strenuous that the dollar would only approach -- but not break -- the T$28 level. -- Alice Hung (2-5080815)
